title: Publish the first firstmate explainer page to GitHub Pages
summary: Render one self-contained HTML page on how firstmate handles work from studies/firstmate-work-handling via a Rust xtask command, and add a GitHub Pages deploy workflow so it opens at a URL. Enabling Pages in repository settings is outside the change and is flagged for the owner.

defaults_applied.how: The renderer is Rust in xtask; the page is generated HTML/CSS with no JS toolchain.
Each page statement cites a claim id and the pinned commit is shown.
Renderer tests added; test, clippy, and fmt must pass.
A short design note records alternatives and deferrals.
The deploy is by workflow; citation and escaping are enforced by tests.
Page and workflow contain no secrets or personal data.
One page and one workflow only.
Page and docs are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: One static page is enough for 'first explainer'; no expert track, replay, or multi-page navigation.
The deploy workflow uses the official GitHub Pages actions, triggered on push to the default branch, and runs the xtask renderer then uploads the output directory.
The Pages source setting (GitHub Actions) must be enabled by the owner in repository settings; the change cannot do that, and the final URL is only confirmed after the first deploy.
The page is rendered only from the validated study JSON (claims, findings, model, pin); no new facts are invented.
The renderer lives in xtask (Rust) with no new heavy dependencies; serde_json is used if already available.

acceptance_criteria.text: An xtask subcommand (e.g. `site`) renders a single self-contained HTML page from studies/firstmate-work-handling JSON, with a viewport meta tag, responsive CSS, and prefers-color-scheme dark mode.
Every factual statement on the page cites a claim id from claims.json, and the page states the pinned firstmate commit from pin.json.
Page text comes from the study data, not hard-coded, and is HTML-escaped.

A new workflow under .github/workflows (named explicitly as a governance change) builds the page with the xtask command and deploys it to GitHub Pages using the official Pages actions with minimal permissions; existing ci.yml is unchanged.

A design note in docs/design records alternatives considered and deferrals (expert track, replay, custom domain); CHANGELOG.md has an entry; README states the one command to build the site locally and where it is published.
The output directory is gitignored or otherwise not committed as build artifacts, and athena.toml, Cargo lints, and rust-toolchain.toml are unchanged.
Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site`; it exits 0 and writes the HTML file; `git status` shows only ignored output.
Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, and `cargo fmt --check`; all pass, including new renderer tests (escaping, claim-id citation, missing-data error).

out_of_scope: Enabling Pages in repository settings or configuring a custom domain
Expert track, replay, quiz, or final report pages
Changing ci.yml, athena.toml, Cargo lints, or toolchain files
departures: Larger than the reference: adds a workflow and a renderer, and the live URL cannot be checked by the verifier, so cost, time, and pass risk are somewhat higher.
